supersedes_note: Rebalanced export of the same 11 pilot pages defined in real_project_pilot_manifest.json (Phase 2.5), which is preserved unchanged. This file does not replace it -- it records the revised per-page export caps used to build a less project-imbalanced 108-group human-review batch, and the resulting distribution.
rebalance_reason: The original flat 'export top 10 per page' rule (Phase 2.5) produced a batch where project_004 (present in 3 of the 11 pilot pages: pilot_04, pilot_05, pilot_12) contributed 28/108 groups (25.9%) versus an ideal even share of ~14.3% across 7 projects. Step 2 of Phase 2.6 flagged this as a real imbalance per the phase spec's explicit instruction to check for single-project domination.

pilot_03.note: capped by availability -- only 14 label groups exist on this page

resulting_distribution.cross_region_contamination_cases: not measurable -- no region/detail-segmentation layer exists (docs/geometry_graph_audit/08_prioritized_roadmap.md P1.4, still open)
resulting_distribution.damaged_or_incomplete_label_cases: not separately flagged in this batch; one confirmed real fraction-splitting example exists on pilot_09 (project_001, page 22) per real_project_error_taxonomy.md #5, whether it landed in this specific 108-group export was not individually re-verified

balance_assessment: After rebalancing, every project's share falls within 13.0%-15.7% of the batch (ideal even split: 14.3%), a maximum deviation of 1.4 percentage points. Not dominated by any single project, page, or page type. Every group in the batch has 2+ real candidates by construction (the difficulty-prioritization rule from Phase 2.5 was preserved) -- this means the batch is NOT representative of the full population's difficulty distribution (which has some zero-candidate and single-candidate groups too, see real_project_pilot_results.md), by deliberate design: the pilot spec asks this batch to prioritize commercially meaningful, difficult cases, not a random sample.
known_limitation: No group in this batch has candidate_count=0, even though pilot_11 was specifically selected as a 'no valid target likely' page and the full population contains 44 such groups (3.5% of 1,253) across all 11 pilot pages. Difficulty-prioritization filled every page's quota with 2+-candidate groups before considering sparse ones. A future export pass could specifically target zero/one-candidate groups if no-valid-target review examples are needed.
